args.title: checkout-api health checks failing after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Service status reported healthy=false with an error rate of ~18%.

Action taken: Rolled production back to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously confirmed healthy in production (v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and also unhealthy). The first rollback attempt failed partway with an orchestrator error, halting after us-east and leaving production in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout successfully to all three regions.

Current state: All regions on v2.3.0, service healthy=true, error rate ~0.2%. v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed until the root cause of the health check failures is identified.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
The incident did go through despite the timeout — **INC-0001** exists, open, SEV2 for checkout-api. No retry needed.

## Summary

**Root problem:** checkout-api was failing health checks in all three production regions on v2.3.1 (`healthy: false`, ~18% error rate).

**Rollback target:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release with a `healthy` status in **production**. I deliberately skipped v2.3.1-rc: although it appears in the release history, it was a staging-only deployment and was itself unhealthy.

**Rollback:**
1. First attempt failed with `partial_failure` — the orchestrator halted after us-east, leaving a genuinely dangerous mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on the broken v2.3.1).
2. Retried, which completed the rollout to all three regions.
3. Verified: all regions on v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened SEV2 **INC-0001** documenting the failing deploy, the partial-failure-and-retry sequence, the final state, and the recommendation not to re-deploy v2.3.1 until the root cause is found.

Two things worth flagging for follow-up:
- The rollback tool reported an error that interrupted a region-by-region rollout. That partial-write behavior is worth investigating on its own — a failed rollback that leaves regions on divergent versions is worse than the original outage in some ways.
- The change-manager approval policy did not apply here, since v2.3.0 has previously been healthy in production. A future *forward* deploy of v2.3.1 (or any never-healthy version) would require change-manager approval.
